Model a Binary Outcome From Sequential Patterns

Source: R/pattern_outcome.R
pattern_outcome.Rd

pattern_outcome() selects the n sequential patterns most associated with a two-valued outcome and fits one logistic regression of the outcome on their presence (or their counts), returning one row per selected pattern with its log odds ratio, odds ratio and Wald interval. It reads any sequence data extract_sequences() reads, takes the outcome from a stored covariate, a vector or each sequence's last state, and can adjust for covariates and add a random intercept per actor.

Each estimate is the association of one pattern with the outcome, adjusted for the other selected patterns and the covariates; it is not a causal effect. The patterns are chosen by their association with the outcome in the same data the model is fitted to, so the p-values do not account for that selection and overstate the evidence: treat them as a ranking, or confirm the selected patterns on new data. A pattern and a longer pattern containing it often occur together, and each coefficient is then adjusted for the other; sequence_patterns() shows how often each pattern occurs, overall and by group.

Usage

pattern_outcome(
  x,
  outcome = "last_obs",
  type = c("ngram", "gapped", "repeated"),
  len = 1:2,
  gap = 1,
  min_freq = 5,
  min_support = 0.01,
  start = NULL,
  end = NULL,
  contain = NULL,
  n = 10,
  priority = "chisq",
  desc = TRUE,
  occurrences = FALSE,
  adjust = NULL,
  adjust_length = FALSE,
  group = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  cols = NULL,
  actor = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

The sequence data, in any form extract_sequences() accepts: prepared data, a long event log, a wide data frame, a netobject, netobject_group or tna model.

outcome

The outcome, with exactly two distinct values: the name of a column stored with the sequences (a covariate of a wide data frame or long event log, or of a network's metadata), or a vector with one value per sequence; use a vector for a model that stores no covariates, such as a tna model. The default, "last_obs", uses each sequence's last observed state as the outcome and removes the states that end some sequence from all sequences, as codyna does; it suits data whose final state codes the outcome, such as an appended "pass" or "fail". An outcome without exactly two values, a vector of the wrong length or a column that is not stored with the sequences raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

type, len, gap, min_freq, min_support, start, end, contain

The pattern definition and filters; see sequence_patterns(). The defaults are codyna's: type = "ngram", len = 1:2, gap = 1, min_freq = 5 and min_support = 0.01. When no pattern passes the filters under both outcome values, an error of class nestimate_no_patterns is raised.

n

The number of patterns entered into the model, a positive whole number. Default 10.

priority

The columns ranking the patterns for selection, applied in order: "chisq" (default), "p_value", "support", "n_sequences", "occurrences", "proportion", "lift" and "length".

desc

Whether each priority column ranks in descending order, recycled to the length of priority. Default TRUE, so "p_value" needs desc = FALSE to select the smallest p-values.

occurrences

Whether each pattern enters the model as its number of occurrences in the sequence instead of its presence (0/1). Default FALSE.

adjust

Covariate columns added to the model. Default NULL. A name that is not a column stored with the sequences raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

adjust_length

Whether to add the number of observed states per sequence as a covariate. Default FALSE, as in codyna.

group

The column identifying the actor (or other cluster) each sequence belongs to; it adds a random intercept per group. It needs lme4, otherwise an error of class nestimate_no_lme4 is raised. Default NULL. A name that is not a column stored with the sequences raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

reference

The reference outcome value; the odds ratios are for the other value. Default NULL, the first value in sorted order; a value that does not occur raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

ci_level

The confidence level of the Wald intervals, a number between 0 and 1. Default 0.95.

cols

The state columns of a wide data frame; see extract_sequences(). Default NULL.

actor, action, time

The actor, action and timestamp columns of a long event log, as in extract_sequences(): setting action declares x an event log. Default NULL.

...

Further arguments passed to prepare() for a long event log, such as time_threshold or order.

Value

A data frame with one row per selected pattern, ordered by pattern name, with the columns pattern, length, occurrences, n_sequences, support and lift (as in sequence_patterns()); the share of the sequences of each outcome value that contain the pattern (support_<value>); chisq (the selection statistic); estimate (the log odds ratio, adjusted for the other terms), std_error, ci_lower, ci_upper and p_value (Wald z); and odds_ratio, or_lower and or_upper.

Sequences with a missing outcome, covariate or group are dropped with a warning of class nestimate_missing_outcome. A selected pattern collinear with the other terms gets NA estimates (and NA standard error, intervals, p-value and odds ratios), its descriptive columns kept, and a warning of class nestimate_aliased_pattern. Warnings from the model fit (such as separation) are passed on unchanged.

Details

pattern_outcome() reproduces codyna::analyze_outcome(): the same pattern discovery and filters, the same ranking and the same model, so the coefficients agree. The steps:

  1. Patterns are found as in sequence_patterns() and filtered by min_freq, min_support, start, end and contain. Patterns absent from all sequences of one outcome value are dropped.

  2. Each pattern gets the chi-square statistic of the number of sequences containing it under each outcome value, against an equal split across the values (codyna's statistic; it does not weight by the size of each outcome group).

  3. The top n patterns by priority enter one model, outcome ~ adjust + pattern_1 + ... + pattern_n, as presence indicators (or occurrence counts with occurrences = TRUE). Ties keep codyna's order: more occurrences first, then first appearance. With group, a random intercept per group is added (lme4::glmer()); otherwise the model is a plain glm().

References

Saqr, M., Tikka, S., & López-Pernas, S. (2026). codyna: Complex Dynamic Systems. R package version 1.0.0.

See also

sequence_patterns
